note: Track guitar-melodies (guitar-scales), step 5: a tune in Dorian made from a four-note motive on the improvisation panel, ended on the root over a drone, then played over the 1st and 4th chords on a backing track. The key is now moves (any key), named only as {{=key}}; the chords are tokens counted the long way once, the position is described before it is played, and each block has one feel to reach. missing: the tune book behind the melody shape is major only, so there is no written modal tune to play from tab; the player makes one up.

exercise.title: Make up a Dorian tune
exercise.why: A tune sounds Dorian when it rests on the root and passes through the raised 6th, so a short motive that ends on one and touches the other keeps the mode however you turn it round.

cells.text:
The panel below spells a short motive in {{=key}} Dorian, then the same four notes reversed, mirrored and rotated. Under it is the neck with the position of {{=key}} Dorian that has {{1}} on the A string: each dot is a note to play. Play the Motive row on the neck.
Then play the Reversed row and the Mirrored row.
Practice until you can play each row straight after reading it.

Press Play below to start the drone on {{=key}}. On the neck below, make up a two-bar tune that passes through the ringed {{6}} and ends on {{1}}.
Practice until the tune comes out the same each time, then change one note.

cells.heading: The tune over the backing track

cells.text:
The backing track moves between two chords of {{=key}} Dorian. {{chord:i7}} is the 1st chord of the key, built on {{1}}. {{chord:IV7}} is the 4th chord, built on {{4}}.
Press Play below to start the backing track. Play your tune over it, then answer it with a second tune that starts on another note.
When {{chord:IV7}} comes round, try holding the ringed {{6}}: it is the 3rd of {{chord:IV7}}, so the Dorian note is the chord's own note there.
{{?key}}In another key the position sits on other frets, and {{6}} is still the 3rd of {{chord:IV7}}.
